headline: 4 dead after bus rams into battery rickshaw in Mirpur
summary: The collision occurred on the Beribadh embankment road near Nawabbagh Uttarpara around 7:30 am on Wednesday.
details: Four people, including two men and two women, were killed after a bus rammed into a battery-powered rickshaw in Dhaka's Mirpur.
The accident took place around 7:30 am on Wednesday on the Beribadh embankment road near Nawabbagh Uttarpara.
The Fire Service and Civil Defence confirmed the casualties and carried out the rescue operation at the scene.
A unit from the Kalyanpur Fire Station was deployed to manage the emergency and recover the victims.
caption:
4 people killed in a horrific collision between a bus and a battery rickshaw in Mirpur.

Four people, including two men and two women, were killed after a bus rammed into a battery-powered rickshaw in Dhaka's Mirpur.

The accident took place around 7:30 am on Wednesday on the Beribadh embankment road near Nawabbagh Uttarpara.

The Fire Service and Civil Defence confirmed the casualties and carried out the rescue operation at the scene.

A unit from the Kalyanpur Fire Station was deployed to manage the emergency and recover the victims.

headline_marked: DB [[detains three labour leaders]] in Ashulia over protest incitement
headline: DB detains three labour leaders in Ashulia over protest incitement
summary: The Detective Branch of police picked up three leaders from different unions over allegations of inciting workers' protests in the industrial area.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of police detained three labour leaders in Ashulia on Tuesday. They are accused of inciting the ongoing workers' protests in the industrial area.
The detainees include Md A Halim of the Jatiya Garments Sramik Federation, Md Shamim of the Bangladesh National Trade Union, and Md Monsur Ali of the Bangladesh Textile Garments Sramik Federation.
According to Saidul Islam, officer-in-charge of the Dhaka District North DB, the detentions were based on credible evidence of the leaders' involvement in inciting the protests.
Md Shamim was detained from the Zirabo area, while Md A Halim and Md Monsur Ali were picked up from the Basundhara Sonia Market area. They will be handed over to Ashulia Police Station.
Khairul Mamun Mintu, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre, condemned the arrests, calling them an attempt to harass the leaders.
Mintu argued that workers' protests cannot be stopped through arrests and attacks, stating that the movement can only be resolved through dialogue with workers.
He further noted that one of the detainees, Md Shamim, was unwell and had contracted dengue fever a few days prior to his detention.
caption:
Three labour leaders detained in Ashulia over allegations of inciting workers' protests.

The Detective Branch (DB) of police detained three labour leaders in Ashulia on Tuesday. They are accused of inciting the ongoing workers' protests in the industrial area.

The detainees include Md A Halim of the Jatiya Garments Sramik Federation, Md Shamim of the Bangladesh National Trade Union, and Md Monsur Ali of the Bangladesh Textile Garments Sramik Federation.

According to Saidul Islam, officer-in-charge of the Dhaka District North DB, the detentions were based on credible evidence of the leaders' involvement in inciting the protests.

Md Shamim was detained from the Zirabo area, while Md A Halim and Md Monsur Ali were picked up from the Basundhara Sonia Market area. They will be handed over to Ashulia Police Station.

Khairul Mamun Mintu, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre, condemned the arrests, calling them an attempt to harass the leaders.

Mintu argued that workers' protests cannot be stopped through arrests and attacks, stating that the movement can only be resolved through dialogue with workers.

He further noted that one of the detainees, Md Shamim, was unwell and had contracted dengue fever a few days prior to his detention.
